O.outcome_detail: positive sense of belonging; elementary students and families

cells.quote: The survey revealed that 65 percent of elementary and 47 percent of secondary Black students and families reported a positive sense of belonging—which are lower reports than all other groups in grades 4 through 12.
cells.note: The study reports a descriptive percentage for Black elementary students and families but does not print an effect size or inferential test.

O.outcome_detail: positive sense of belonging; secondary students and families

cells.quote: The survey revealed that 65 percent of elementary and 47 percent of secondary Black students and families reported a positive sense of belonging—which are lower reports than all other groups in grades 4 through 12.
cells.note: The study reports a descriptive percentage for Black secondary students and families but does not print an effect size or inferential test.

cells.quote: The 2024 PULSE Survey confirmed these findings, maintaining that Black students reported lower scores in having a sense of belonging, as well as identity, agency, and sense of safety, than all other groups in grades 6 through 12.
cells.note: Descriptive survey comparison; no printed effect size.
